texts: good. the moulting trigger and the feathers' fall to the cliff base form one fireable rule, with the base attached to the cliff as its part.
good. the shedding is tied to the moulting occasion, 'onto the base of the cliff' is carried as the destination, and nothing beyond the sentence is asserted.
good. 'the fallen feathers' comes through as a specific set with 'fallen' handed to each feather, and the apprentices' habitual morning collecting is a fireable generic rule.

mixed: the content is all there, but the parse reads 'the Keepers' as a group of people who are keepers and adds a rule making every one of them store the feathers, whereas a capitalized plural name is not supposed to posit members at all — and the same label is read the other way in 'The Keepers tolerate sky-cats.', so the two sentences will not agree on who the Keepers are. If you do mean each Keeper separately, make it explicit: "Each of the Keepers stores the collected feathers in a bin at the Watch."
